newsitem.title: UK: Iveco-Ford closes British plant, 450 jobs go.
newsitem.headline: Iveco-Ford closes British plant, 450 jobs go.

text.p: Commercial vehicle maker Iveco-Ford Truck Ltd., controlled by Iveco of Italy and co-owned by Ford Motor Co., said Friday it will shut its assembly plant at Langley, near London, with the loss of 450 jobs.

Nigel Emms, external relations manager, said the decision followed a strategic review of Iveco's European manufacturing plants in the light of continued overcapacity across the freight vehicle industry.
Manufacturing of all truck ytpes would be transferred to Brescia in northern Italy, he said.

These trucks are in the so-called medium weight segment of the market and, according to Iveco, a unit of Fiat Spa, a recession across the whole market since the late 1980s has hit this sector especially hard while capacity in Europe has continued to exceed demand.
Langley was the main asset of the Iveco-Ford venture when it was established in 1986. Prior to that it had been a Ford commercial vehicle plant since 1960.
Production will cease at the end of May. Emms said the factory had assembled just 7,700 trucks in 1996 compared with 18,000 in 1988, adding there was no sign of a recovery towards that peak level.
